specification.problem: Long-time evolution of a discrete-time quantum walk on a finite graph with dynamic percolation (edges randomly present/absent at each step), modeled as a random unitary channel and analyzed via asymptotics of random unitary maps.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Smallest useful construction: a coined quantum walk on a tiny finite 1D chain (assumed N=3 sites, open boundary) with i.i.d. random edge configurations per step, written as a random unitary channel and its asymptotic (long-time) behavior in background form. The paper's specific solution method, the detailed 1D worked numerical example, the literature review and the 2D Grover-coin results are outside scope.

symbols.domain: positive semidefinite, trace one, on H

equations.label: Random unitary channel
equations.description: One step of the walk averaged over random edge configurations drawn freshly each step.
equations.abstract_quote: the connections appear and disappear randomly in each step during the time evolution
equations.justification: Per-step random connections with open system dynamics imply averaging unitary evolutions; the exact form is the standard random unitary map.

equations.label: Edge configuration probability
equations.description: Probability of configuration omega under independent edge percolation.
equations.justification: Proposed concrete percolation model; the abstract does not specify the distribution.
assumptions: Independent edges with common probability p

equations.label: Step operator
equations.description: Coin then shift restricted to present edges; for blocked edges the walker is reflected (assumed rule).
equations.justification: Standard coined-walk form; the blocked-edge rule is a choice.
assumptions: Reflection at missing edges so U_omega is unitary
C is a coin unitary, e.g. Hadamard in 1D

equations.label: Asymptotic decomposition
equations.description: For a random unitary channel, the asymptotic dynamics lives on the peripheral spectrum. The fixed-point set is the commutant of the set {U_omega} (the unital case). Peripheral eigenvalues give rotating components.
equations.justification: Known results on random unitary maps; the paper's specific treatment is not reconstructed here.
assumptions: Possible non-fixed peripheral eigenvalues give a periodic limit, so the limit may be taken along subsequences

equations.label: Peripheral eigen-equation
equations.description: Peripheral eigenoperators of a random unitary channel satisfy a common covariance condition for all configurations.
equations.justification: Standard property of unital channels with Kraus unitaries; determines the asymptotic subspace.
assumptions: Strictly positive weights on the included configurations

registers.name: coin
registers.size: 1 qubit per site, or direction space of dimension 2

specification.initial_state: Assumed localized state |x_0>|c_0> on the middle site with a fixed coin state, rho_0=|psi_0><psi_0|.

steps.description: Fix the tiny instance, the coin, and the edge probability p, and enumerate the configurations Omega and their weights.
Build the unitaries U_omega and the averaged channel Phi.
Find the fixed points and the peripheral spectrum of Phi (commutant condition) to obtain the asymptotic state.

specification.classical_postprocessing: Numerical diagonalization of the superoperator Phi to obtain the peripheral eigenspace and the limiting position distribution; not a quantum measurement procedure.
assumptions: No scope was given, so a 3-site open chain with a Hadamard coin and independent edge percolation is chosen as the smallest instance
Equations eq_4 and eq_5 are textbook background, not the paper's results
No claim is made about the paper's actual method or numerical example
